items.title: NOT a singularity: an infinitely thin donut! #shorts
items.summary: This is where you need to tear up everything you think you know about black holes. Because for a rotating black hole, you don’t have a singularity, you have a ring singularity. An infinitely thin donu…
items.body:
This is where you need to tear up everything you think you know about black holes.

Because for a rotating black hole, you don’t have a singularity, you have a ring singularity. An infinitely thin donut. That’s because of the forces at play because the black hole is spinning, throwing the matter outwards.

It’s a similar process to what you feel holding hands with a friend and spinning around. You feel thrown backwards. It’s what makes Earth not a perfect sphere but an oblate spheroid, slightly squashed and bulging at the equator. Saturn spinning faster is even more squashed. Take that to the extreme for black holes and you end up with a ring shaped singularity. That some people like to portmanteau and call a ringularity. Those people are psychos.

items.title: Is falling into a black hole fast or slow? #shorts
items.summary: When you’re falling into a black hole, how long does it take after you cross the event horizon of a black hole, that sphere of no return, before you reach the singularity? The place where all the matt…
items.body:
When you’re falling into a black hole, how long does it take after you cross the event horizon of a black hole, that sphere of no return, before you reach the singularity?

The place where all the matter is crushed down into an infinitely dense infinitely small region of space.

How long it actually takes to reach the singularity after becoming trapped beyond the event horizon depends on how massive the black hole is. So for a black hole the same mass as the Sun, it’s a few microseconds, but for a more massive black hole it's longer because the event horizon is also larger. So it's around a minute for the black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, and a few hours for a supermassive black hole billions of times heavier than the Sun.

And rather counterintuitively, if you tried to resist the pull of singularity once you’re past the event horizon, by accelerating away from it, for example if you were in a spacecraft firing your engines, that would actually mean you reached the singularity sooner. Because time and space swap inside a black hole. And the singularity becomes a moment in time, a moment in your future, rather than a place in space. So if you accelerate, in whatever direction, in your frame of reference, you get there sooner.

At least, that’s the simplified picture of a black hole, the one we all tend to learn about. But real black holes also spin. And that changes everything. Including the nature of the singularity itself, which becomes a donut shape.

At least, an infinitely thin donut. Which does even weirder things to time.

items.body:
Discover Odoo 👉 https://www.odoo.com/r/EgUR
The first app is free for life. Thanks to Odoo for sponsoring this video!

Support another year of kurzgesagt with a brand new 12,027 Human Era Calendar: https://shop.kgs.link/calendar27
You get twelve months of human-made artwork for your walls, and we get to keep creating free, high-quality videos for everyone. Sound good? 👉👈

Sources & further reading:
https://sites.google.com/view/sources-cisplatin/

Hi! I am Philipp Dettmer, the founder of kurzgesagt, and back in 2018, I was being treated for a stage 3 B testicular cancer. This was a very serious situation, but it is not a sad story! In fact, going through chemotherapy was one of the most interesting experiences of my life. I was treated with Cisplatin, which, in a nutshell, put my body through a controlled medical violence. This toxic chemotherapy agent is a hero and a villain of this story, but it absolutely saved my life.
So what exactly is Cisplatin, and what was my body going through during the treatment?

items.summary: Order the S50 Pro: https://upf.ai/0x06lj7k What can the Seestar S50 Pro capture when you give it three nights on the same target? In this video, I put this smart telescope to work on a multi-night ast…
items.body:
Order the S50 Pro: https://upf.ai/0x06lj7k

What can the Seestar S50 Pro capture when you give it three nights on the same target? In this video, I put this smart telescope to work on a multi-night astrophotography project to see how far I could take the final image.

Collecting more light is one of the most rewarding ways to improve your deep-sky images. This project was a chance to slow down, revisit the same patch of sky, and see what a small telescope could reveal with a little patience.

I’ll share my experience using the Seestar S50 Pro over three nights and the resulting image. If you’re interested in smart telescopes, beginner astrophotography, or getting more out of your Seestar, this video is for you.
